CVE-2020-16156.note: Fixed in the CPAN client 2.29, hardened further in 2.33 (Perl 5.36 and later); Perl 5.44 contains both. The cpan tool is not used on the phone.

CVE-2020-23109.note: Upstream analysis and Debian place the fix in libheif 1.7.0 (commit bca0162); the installed 1.23.7 contains it. Upstream never named an exact release, so this rests on that analysis.

CVE-2020-23922.note: The bug was only in the gif2rgb command-line tool, not in the GIF library. It was fixed upstream in giflib 5.2.2, and the installed package does not contain gif2rgb at all.

CVE-2020-27748.note: xdg-email 1.2.1 still turns attach= in a mailto: link into a Thunderbird attachment, so a crafted link could add a file such as a key to a new e-mail; the upstream fix (passing attachments separately) is in no release yet. Thunderbird is the mail app here, but nothing on the phone hands links from elsewhere to xdg-email: browsers and Flatpak apps open mailto: through GIO or the portal, which start Thunderbird directly, and Muga calls it only with --attach for the pictures you chose. It only matters if you run xdg-email yourself with a link from someone else; check the attachments in the compose window before sending.

CVE-2021-31879.note: wget 1.25.0 still sends a user-given Authorization or Cookie header on to another host after a redirect; the fix is upstream but in no release yet. Nothing on the phone runs wget with login details, so it only matters if you do that yourself (use --max-redirect 0 then).

CVE-2021-3575.note: Fixed upstream in OpenJPEG 2.5.1; the installed 2.5.4 contains the fix. The bug was in the opj_decompress command-line tool, not in the library that apps use.

CVE-2021-36770.note: Only Encode 3.05 to 3.11 were affected; fixed in Encode 3.12. The installed Perl 5.44 ships Encode 3.24.

CVE-2021-3773.note: The weakness ("port shadow") is in the NAT of a VPN server that several clients share: another client of the same server can find out or redirect a victim's connection. It is not a bug in OpenVPN, and there is no kernel fix; the protection belongs on the server. The phone uses OpenVPN only as a client (no OpenVPN server and no server configuration), so nothing on this system can be attacked this way. Whether a VPN you connect to is safe depends on how its provider set up the server.

CVE-2026-72493.note: Use-after-free when a packet passes the netif_running() check in enqueue_to_backlog() before the backlog lock and escapes the flush while the device is unregistered. The 6.1 kernels of this phone (UT's 6.1.145 and plinius-kernel 6.1.177) still check it after rps_lock_irqsave(), which is the state the fix restores, so the race window does not exist. The kernel CNA marks every version since 4.2 as affected because it names the commit that introduced the check.

CVE-2025-38675.note: The CNA lists this as unfixed in 6.1 since the backport of the hash pointer lookup in 6.1.191. In the kernel of this project xfrm_state_find() fills state_ptrs right after rcu_read_lock(), before any path that uses it, and 6.1 has no per-CPU state cache that could jump ahead (checked in the source of plinius-kernel 6.1.192-19).

CVE-2026-64017.note: Fixed in 6.1.191; the CNA also names a second backport in 6.1.75 without a fix in this branch. The kernel of this project has the corrected blk_mq_submit_bio(): the cached request is taken off the plug list before anything can sleep (checked in the source of plinius-kernel 6.1.192-19).

CVE-2023-54164.note: A locking race in Bluetooth ISO sockets (LE Audio). The main fix is in 6.1.42; the CNA also names an older backport without a fix in this branch. ISO sockets are not active on the phone: the kernel only registers them when the experimental ISO feature is switched on through the Bluetooth management interface, which needs root, and BlueZ does not do it (Experimental and KernelExperimental are off; no /proc/net/bluetooth/iso, checked 2026-11-18).

CVE-2026-74531.note: The code with the bug, abort_conn_sync() queued with a pointer to the connection, is not in this kernel: in its 6.1 source hci_abort_conn() sends the disconnect itself, and the management interface queues the abort by connection handle and looks the connection up again (checked in plinius-kernel 6.1.192-19).

CVE-2026-31648.note: The overflow is in the nr_pages calculation of filemap_map_pages() for large folios in newer kernels. The 6.1 code of this kernel maps one page at a time and has no such calculation (checked in plinius-kernel 6.1.192-19).

CVE-2026-23451.note: The endless loop is in the bonding driver, which this kernel does not build (CONFIG_BONDING is not set); the other files of the fix only change an interface for it.

CVE-2026-74753.note: A use-after-free through perf event groups. The fix is not in this kernel, but perf_event_open() is refused to every program except root: kernel.perf_event_paranoid is 3 (Android's restriction), measured on the phone 2026-11-18 as the normal user (Permission denied).

CVE-2026-68085.note: The fix is not in this kernel. The bug is in the Bluetooth UART line discipline, which can only be attached to a terminal with CAP_NET_ADMIN in the initial namespace, so by root. The phone does not use it: its Bluetooth reaches the kernel through bluebinder as a virtual controller (vhci).

CVE-2024-58241.note: The fix (it uses disable_work, which 6.1 does not have) is not in this kernel. The race only occurs while a Bluetooth controller is being removed. The phone's controller is a virtual one (vhci) that bluebinder, a root service, opens for the Android Bluetooth HAL; it only goes away when bluebinder stops, and only root can open /dev/vhci.

CVE-2025-68304.note: A race in the Bluetooth receive path: data arriving on a connection while it is being torn down can use the freed connection. The fix (a rework of the receive path in five files) is not in this kernel. On the phone the teardown that can race with it only happens when Bluetooth is switched off or a device is disconnected or unpaired in the settings: plinius-kernel's plinius-btsuspend keeps the links at suspend. So an attacker has to be connected already and send data at the very moment the user drops the connection; no exploit is known.

CVE-2025-39965.note: Allocating an IPsec SPI could hand out 0, and such a state is later used after it was freed. Any program on the phone can reach it: it can create its own user namespace and in it IPsec states (measured 2026-11-18 as the normal user), so this is a possible way to root for a malicious app. Fixed in plinius-kernel 6.1.192-20.

CVE-2026-53132.note: A vsock connection can be fed empty messages that are queued without limit, and the vsock loopback transport is built in, so any program on the phone can make the kernel use up memory until the system stalls. No access to data or control of the phone. Fixed in plinius-kernel 6.1.192-20.

CVE-2024-27005.note: The interconnect core could walk a node's request list while another path changed it. The bug came with the 6.1.y backport of "interconnect: Fix locking for runpm vs reclaim"; linux-6.1.193 fixes it by reverting that backport. plinius-kernel already has the upstream fix instead (path_init() changes the list under icc_bw_lock, from android14-6.1), and the vendor kernel 6.1.145 never had the backport. The revert is not taken: it would remove a lock this kernel still uses.

extra.note: Use-after-free in the IPv4 TCP handshake: a SYN with IP options sent to a listening IPv4 TCP port can crash the kernel and possibly lead to remote code execution. Fixed upstream in 6.1.190; the vendor kernel 6.1.145 and the kernel source of this project do not contain the fix. The published root exploit needs an MPTCP listener, which this kernel cannot provide (no MPTCP). The only IPv4 listener reachable from outside is SSH, and its firewall chain admits only USB and private networks on Wi-Fi, hotspot and USB Ethernet, never mobile data. So an attacker has to be in the same local network.
